note: Example catalog (a demonstration, not anyone's real skills): every entry point of the example skills declared as a typed operation. 'doc' says where the command and its exit codes are written. 'declared_against' is the md5 each skill had when its declarations were checked; after a skill changes, check its declarations again and run `python3 -m herdr_py.ontology pin`.

conditions.python3: a Python 3.6+ interpreter (the one running the ontology)
conditions.loopback: can open a port on 127.0.0.1 and connect to it
conditions.git: git, to hand files to another machine

interfaces.static-site: a folder with index.html that a static server can serve
interfaces.web-url: a URL a browser can open

notes-md.description: a notes file: headings and paragraphs

site.description: a one-page site made from notes

local-url.description: a URL of a server on this machine (valid only here)

public-url.description: a URL on the public host

builder.source: declared: a build container that cannot open ports a browser could reach

workstation.source: probed on this machine when the ontology is built

operations.doc: Python's http.server serves the folder it runs in; started in the background and stopped when the chain ends

operations.manual: the owner copies the site to the public host under TARGET
commit the files, push the branch and go on in a session on the workstation

notes-site-builder.description: Turn notes into a site that passes the lint and answers in a browser, starting in a build container

notes-site-workstation.description: The same, starting on the workstation
